The provided text discusses a legal case, *Carter vs. Pearson*, focusing on the admissibility of a written confession. The evidence presented includes the confession itself and phone records indicating repeated calls from unknown sources to Pearson around the time of the signing. The relevance of this evidence is high to the specific legal matter at hand, as it directly supports the defense's claim that the confession was obtained under duress. The phone records serve as corroborating circumstantial evidence for the alleged threats, which is a critical factor in determining whether the confession was voluntary and thus admissible in court.
